services.name: Microsoft Exchange Server
services.description: On-premises enterprise mail and calendaring server

threatContext.remote-command-execution: Pre-auth RCE chains against internet-facing OWA/ECP/EWS: ProxyLogon (CVE-2021-26855 SSRF + CVE-2021-27065), ProxyShell (CVE-2021-34473/34523/31207), ProxyNotShell (CVE-2022-41040/41082), leading to webshell drop in the OWA/ECP virtual directories
threatContext.unpatched-vulnerabilities: Exchange servers running behind on cumulative updates and security updates, unpatched OWA/ECP/EWS front-end exposed to the internet, legacy Exchange 2013/2016 past end of support
threatContext.account-takeover: Password spraying and credential stuffing against OWA, EWS, ActiveSync, and Autodiscover, MFA bypass via legacy protocols (IMAP/POP/SMTP AUTH), phishing for mailbox credentials
threatContext.credential-theft: NTLM relay from Exchange (PrivExchange / EWS PushSubscription forcing authentication), harvesting cached credentials from a compromised server, capturing OWA form-based logon credentials via a webshell
threatContext.data-exfiltration: Mailbox export via New-MailboxExportRequest to PST, EWS bulk mail download, transport/journaling rules silently forwarding mail externally, searching all mailboxes with a compromised admin role
threatContext.privilege-escalation: Exchange servers holding high privileges in AD (WriteDACL on the domain via legacy Exchange permissions) enabling escalation to Domain Admin, ECP admin abuse, elevation from webshell running as SYSTEM
threatContext.lateral-movement: Pivoting from a compromised Exchange server into Active Directory, using Exchange service accounts and NTLM relay to reach domain controllers and other hosts

remote-command-execution: Publish OWA/ECP/EWS behind a reverse proxy or VPN with pre-authentication rather than exposing them directly to the internet
Apply Exchange Security Updates immediately for actively exploited chains and run the Exchange Health Checker and EOMT/MSERT
Restrict access to the ECP and PowerShell virtual directories to admin networks only, and monitor for webshells in the virtual-directory paths
unpatched-vulnerabilities: Keep Exchange on the latest Cumulative Update and apply Security Updates within an emergency SLA for internet-facing servers
Migrate off end-of-support Exchange versions (2013/2016) to a supported release or Exchange Online
Run the Exchange Server Health Checker and subscribe to MSRC advisories for Exchange CVEs
account-takeover: Enforce MFA on OWA and ECP via AD FS or a reverse proxy, and disable legacy authentication protocols (IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH, Basic Auth)
Configure account lockout and monitor Windows/IIS logs for password spray against OWA, EWS, and Autodiscover
Deploy Exchange behind a pre-authenticating gateway and restrict external client protocols to those that support modern auth
credential-theft: Mitigate NTLM relay (PrivExchange) by removing excessive Exchange AD permissions, enabling LDAP signing and channel binding, and applying EWS throttling
Enforce SMB signing and Extended Protection for Authentication on Exchange virtual directories
Run Exchange with least-privilege service accounts and monitor for anomalous EWS PushSubscription and authentication events
data-exfiltration: Restrict the Mailbox Import Export RBAC role to break-glass accounts and alert on New-MailboxExportRequest usage
Audit and alert on new transport rules, journaling rules, and mailbox forwarding to external domains
Enable mailbox and admin audit logging and forward Exchange/IIS logs to a SIEM to detect bulk EWS downloads
privilege-escalation: Apply the Exchange split-permissions model and remove legacy WriteDACL/high privileges Exchange holds over the domain object
Place Exchange servers in a hardened tier and restrict which accounts can administer ECP and Exchange PowerShell
Monitor for privilege changes and webshell-spawned processes running as SYSTEM/NetworkService on Exchange hosts
lateral-movement: Segment Exchange servers from workstations and restrict outbound connections from Exchange to only required domain controllers and services
Enforce LDAP channel binding/signing and SMB signing to block NTLM relay pivoting to domain controllers
Use least-privilege service accounts and monitor east-west traffic from Exchange with EDR and network detection
